title: Rutile production provenance v1
description: Derived build provenance binding a production candidate to its source tree, toolchain, exact enabled cargo features, reproducibility controls, and candidate artifact hash. The candidate_sha256 is always measured from the candidate artifact file. The reproducibility controls have an explicit derivation boundary recorded by controls_origin: when it is 'ambient_build_env' the operator asserts the candidate was produced under the recorded controls and the generator measured them from the inherited build environment; when it is 'operator_re_derivation' the controls were re-derived from the repository (commit-date SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and repo-derived RUSTFLAGS) rather than measured from the candidate build subprocess. A production candidate must originate from a clean tree, must not enable the test-control feature, and must remap path prefixes for reproducibility.

source_tag.description: Clean detached signed tag naming this release (for example v0.2.0). Optional; absent when the candidate is built from an untagged commit.

built_at.description: ISO-8601 build completion timestamp, for example 2026-07-14T00:00:00Z.

features.description: Exactly the cargo features enabled on the candidate build, in canonical order. The test-control feature must be absent: it gates instrumented test-only lifecycle behavior and is forbidden in production artifacts.

controls_origin.description: Explicit reproducibility-controls derivation boundary. candidate_sha256 is always measured from the candidate file; this field records whether the reproducibility controls (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH + --remap-path-prefix + target_root) were measured from the ambient build environment or re-derived from the repository by an operator assertion. A self-injected re-derivation must not be mistaken for an independent build-environment measurement.
